Concession

/kun-SESH-un/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Concession means something granted or given up, especially in response to demands, in order to reach an agreement or end a dispute.

The company's offer of three extra vacation days was the concession that finally persuaded the union to sign the new contract.

Worked Example

Hoping to end the curfew standoff, Talia's parents offered a concession: she could stay out an hour later on weekends if she took over the morning dog-walking.

The parents gave up something they originally wanted — the earlier curfew — in response to Talia's requests, in order to reach an agreement. That specific thing one side gives up is the concession.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

accommodation: an adjustment made to satisfy someone's needs

allowance: something granted or permitted

trade-off: giving up one thing to gain another

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

demand: an insistent claim that something be given

ultimatum: a final demand with no room to bargain

Where it sits · how much ground you yield — gesture → concession → surrender

gesture vs. concession: A gesture is weaker than a concession — a gesture is a small token of goodwill that costs little, while a concession means actually giving up something you wanted.

surrender vs. concession: Surrender is stronger than a concession — surrender means giving up everything and abandoning the fight, while a concession gives ground on one point to keep the agreement moving.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — con-

Prefix — con-: together; also used to intensify, 'wholly'

Root — cess

Root — cess: to go, to yield (Latin cedere, past stem cess-)

Suffix — -ion

Suffix — -ion: the act or result of

Put it together

Put it together: A concession is literally 'the act of yielding altogether' — the Latin root cedere pictures one side stepping back, giving ground so the two sides can move closer to a deal.

Use the root in a new word: cede

Use the root in a new word: cede: After the war, the kingdom agreed to cede the border valley to its neighbor — formally yielding the land it once claimed.

Root Check

Word Choice

Formal — negotiation and political register

A concession is one side's specific give: the thing granted or surrendered to move a deal forward. The overall settlement in which both sides give ground is a compromise — a compromise is usually built out of several concessions, at least one from each side. Bonus sense with the same root idea of 'something granted': a 'concession stand' at a ballpark is a small business granted the right to sell food there.
